la:pron:ecquis.gloss: Is there anyone who...?, Is there anybody who...?
senses: Is there anyone who...?, Is there anybody who...?
la:pron:ecquis.html:
ecquis, ecquid (abl. ecqui,
v.infra, II. B.), pron. interrog. subst., Is there any one who? Any, any one, any body, any thing? in impassioned interrogation, i. q. num quis, quid (class.).
Prop.: aperite hoc: heus, ecquis hic est? ecquis hoc aperit ostium?; so, ecquis,; ; et saep.; ; ; ; : ecquid,; ; ; ; ; ; :

eccui, : ecquem,; Cael. in et saep.— With suffix nam, ; ; ; : quid huc tantum hominum incedunt? ecquidnam afferunt?.—

Adj. for ecqui: ecquis alius Sosia intu'st,; ; ; ; ; —
Hence, derivv. the adverbs,
ecquid, i. q. numquid, num, whether, perchance, in direct and indirect interrogation: ecquid audis?Do you hear?; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. with tandem,: Tr. Ecquid placent (aedes)? Th. Ecquid placeant me rogas? ; ; ; ; ; ; .—Rarely (like quid) for cur, .—*
ecqui, i. q. num aliqui, whether? in indirect interrog.: coepi observare, ecqui majorem filius mi honorem haberet, etc., whether, etc., (but the true reading, , and , is ecquid, v. Draeger, Hist Synt. I. p. 318).—
ec-quo, i. q. num aliquo, anywhere? ecquo te tua virtus provexisset? ecquo industria? , cf. on these adverbs Hand, Turs. II. pp. 351-355.

la:other:ecce.gloss: see!, look!, behold!, points out something with emphasis
senses: see!, look!, behold!, points out something with emphasis
here!, or here am/are/is!; used to denote that something is present (compare French voici or Italian ecco)
la:other:ecce.html:
ecce,
adv. demonstr. [perh. from locat. form of pronom. stem i, with demonstr. ending -ce; hence, in comedy often scanned ĕce, Corss. Aussp. 2, 636, 1026 sq. —Ribbeck explains ecce as indef. form ec, as in ecquis, ecquando, etc., strengthened by demonstr. ce, Lat. Part. p. 42 sq.; and Curt. refers it to root oc- of oculus; cf. eccere, Gr. Etym. p. 457], points out an object with emphasis, lo! see! behold! (constr. class. with nom. or clause, and ante-class. also with acc.).
In gen.: quem quaero, optime ecce obviam mihi est,behold! there comes he I was wishing for,: ecce autem video rure redeuntem senem,: ecce Dionaei processit Caesaris astrum,: ecce trahebatur passis Priameïa virgo Crinibus,; cf. ; ; sometimes in the middle of a clause: audiat haec tantum—vel qui venit ecce Palaemon,; : apparet adhuc vetus cicatrix,; —
In partic.
To denote that something is present (cf. Fr. voici), here (in this sense mostly ellipt.): circus noster ecce adest, Plaut Fragm. ap. Müll.; so with adest,; : quid me quaeris? ... ecce me,here I am,; so, ecce me,; ; : ecce nos,: ecce odium meum,: ecce Gripi scelera,: ecce tuae litterae de Varrone,: ecce hominem te, Stasime, nihili,; and simply ecce,here I am,.—
In enumerations, or after other objects mentioned, to introduce a new one with emphasis (Ciceronian): consecuti sunt hos Critias, Theramenes, Lysias, etc. ... ecce tibi exortus est Isocrates, Cic de Or. 2, 22 fin.; ; ; so ellipt.,; ; .—
To introduce something unexpected or strange; hence, sometimes connected with subito, repente, de improviso, etc.: ecce Apollo mihi ex oraculo imperat, Ut, etc.,; ; : et ecce de improviso ad nos accedit cana veritas, Varr. ap. ; cf. : discubitum noctu ut imus, ecce ad me advenit mulier,; so with a preceding cum, ; with dum: haec dum agit, ecce, etc.,; with ubi, .—Ellipt.: ecce postridie Cassio litterae Capua a Lucretio,; ; ; with subito, ; ; cf.: ecce autem repente,; and with a preceding cum, ; — For the expression ecce autem, v. autem. —
In conversat. lang., combined with the pronouns is, ille, and iste, into one word standing for either the simple ecce, or the pronoun itself, but with demonstrative force, in the foll. forms: nom., ecca, ; ; : eccilla,: eccillud,: acc. sing., eccum, ; ; et saep.; ; et saep.; Titin. ap. P.: eccam,; ; et saep.; ; : eccillum,; ; ; and syncopated ellum,; ; : eccillam, and sync. ellam,; ; ; eccistam,: plur., eccos, ; ; ; ; ; ; Afran. ap. P.: eccas,: ecca,.

—On the construction of eccum, etc., cf. Brix ad ; and on ecce see Hand, Turs. II. pp. 343-351.

la:noun:ecclesia.html:
ecclēsĭa (ēcclĕsĭa, ; Venant. Carm. 3, 6, 24; and ĕclĕsĭa, ; ), ae, f., = ἐκκλησία,
an assembly of the (Greek) people.
Prop.: et ecclesia consentiente, senate and people, in the free cities of Greece: bule et ecclesia, Plin. et Traj. Ep. 111, 1. —
Transf.
In eccl. Lat.
A religious assembly of Christians, a Christian congregation, a church (eccl. Lat.; very freq.): die ecclesiae, etc.,; ; .—
The Church, the whole body of believers: Christus dilexit ecclesiam,: Dei,; ; so, in coelo,.—
A Christian place of assembly, a church: ut nomine ecclesiae, id est populi qui continetur, significamus locum qui continet,; cf. also ; —
An assembly, a meeting in gen., .

Lit.: filius David,i. e. Solomon,.—

la:noun:echinus.html:
ĕchīnus, i, m., = ἐχῖνος,
a hedgehog, urchin.
Prop., usually the (edible) sea-urchin, Echinus esculentus, Linn.; Müll.; Afran. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; .—The land-urchin (otherwise called erinaceus), ; cf. .—
Transf., of things having a similar shape.
A copper vessel for the table, perh. to wash out the cups in, a rinsing-bowl, , v. Heindorf, ad h. l.; .—
The prickly husk of a chestnut, ; .—
In archit., an ornament under the chapiter of a Doric or Ionic column, an echinus, ; ; cf. Müller, Archaeol. § 277.

la:noun:ecloga.gloss: A short passage of writing from a longer work; an excerpt.
senses: A short passage of writing from a longer work; an excerpt.
la:noun:ecloga.html:
eclŏga, ae, f., = ἐκλογή,
a selection, consisting of the finest passages, from a written composition.
In gen.: eclogas ex Annali descriptas, Varr. ap. P.—
In partic., a short poem of any kind, like the poems in the Sylvae of Statius; cf. ; praef.; the Idyls of Ausonius; cf. ; the Odes of Horace, praef., and in many MSS. of Horace; and in the grammarians the Bucolica of Vergil are also called Eclogae, Eclogues; cf. Heyne de Carm. Bucol. in Verg. Opp. ed. Wagn. I. p. 18.
